methods.description: Start a new workflow execution of a registered type. Requires `type` (the registered workflow type name) and accepts an optional `input` payload plus start options: `id` (client-supplied workflow id), `executionTimeout`, `startAt`/`startAfter` (mutually exclusive scheduling), `tags`, `idempotencyKey` (at-most-once dedup: a repeated key returns the existing run instead of starting a second), and `searchAttributes`. Faults with InvalidParams for an unregistered type or malformed options, and Conflict when a workflow with the same id already exists or the supplied `idempotencyKey` has been spent (its run was purged or swept by retention).

methods.description: Start a workflow or deliver a signal to it if it already exists (signal-with-start). An absent target is created and delivered the signal in one batch; a non-terminal target (running, pending, or suspended) is signalled; a terminal target faults with Conflict unless `onTerminalConflict: "start-new"` is supplied with `id` and `signalId`, in which case the prior terminal run is replaced through the shared terminal-replacement path and the initial signal is delivered to the fresh run. A spent `idempotencyKey` whose run was purged or swept by retention also faults with Conflict. A signal name the target declares no signal for, when it declares its signals, faults with Unprocessable. Requires `type`, `signalName`, and exactly one of `signalId` or `idempotencyKey` (not both). Accepts `input`, `signalPayload`, and the non-idempotency start options from weft.workflows.start (`id`, `executionTimeout`, `startAt`/`startAfter`, `tags`, `searchAttributes`) plus `onTerminalConflict`; `idempotencyKey` is governed by the "exactly one of" rule above and cannot be combined with restart. Returns the workflow `id`. Concurrent callers converge on one workflow and one signal only with a shared `idempotencyKey`, or a shared `id` plus `signalId`; a bare `signalId` (no `id`/`idempotencyKey`) starts a fresh run per caller and does not converge.

methods.description: Skip one upcoming run of a recurring schedule by `scheduleId`: the occurrence named by `occurrence` (milliseconds since the epoch), the next run or any after it, starts no workflow, and the runs around it fire as usual. Omitted, the next run is skipped, whichever it is. In a time zone the next wake-up can be the end of a daylight-saving gap that starts nothing, so the next run is the next real one; a run that is due but has not started is the next run. Skipped runs are listed as `skippedOccurrences` on the schedule until it moves past them, and `weft.schedules.unskip` takes one back. The skip leaves `revision` and `nextFireAt` as they are, and skipping a run already skipped changes nothing. A paused schedule accepts a skip of its runs counted from the first after now, and keeps it for when it is resumed. A fire moves neither `revision` nor `status`, so the run a caller read can start before the skip is written: the skip is refused with Conflict (reason `occurrence-not-next`) when `occurrence` is not an upcoming run as the write lands, whether a fire passed it or the cadence starts no run then. A schedule keeps at most 100 skipped runs, and one more is a Conflict. Pass `expectedRevision` to refuse the skip with StaleRevision when the schedule has changed since it was read; the revision is checked first. Faults with NotFound when no schedule with the given id exists, and with Conflict when the schedule is cancelled.
